correctness.rationale: For B>0 the positive-branch matrix A is exact with A^4=-4I and det A=2. Centering at p_B turns every strict survivor test into r_j u>-B. The first seven supporting halfplanes define a bounded seven-vertex polygon of area 79B^2/128, by exact pairwise-line intersections and the shoelace formula. For n>=6 the shifted conditions j=1 and j=7 imply j=0, yielding exact S_(n+1)-p=A^-1(S_n-p). An explicit rational counterexample shows this cannot hold when n<=5; the preceding bounded set S_5 has area 5B^2/4 and the first ratio is 79/160, not 1/2. Determinant induction gives 79B^2/2^(n+1) for all n>=6, hence geometric first-exit law when sampling uniformly from S_6, with tau=7+k having mass 2^(-k-1), mean 8. A^-8=I/16 forces the infinite survivor to be the fixed point. The actual exact-rational checker reproduced the identities for n=6 through 18; finite checks are not the infinite proof. Strict boundary conditions are preserved.

value.rationale: The model and strict branch switch are natural to the original Selkov ultradiscretization: excursion length before the first switch controls transient time near its expanding branch. The theorem provides a full-plane (not Poincaré-line) survival-area law, a complete exact heptagon and a sharp normalizing constant, for every finite time after the sharp seven-tested-coordinate stage (n=6) at which a one-step geometric renewal starts, unlike n=5. Its exact geometric first-exit distribution is a substantial quantitative dynamical statistic complementary to the earlier limit-cycle/stability and measure-zero basin descriptions, not an arbitrary slice or routine re-expression of a known number. It does not assert generality beyond the studied model.
